fix.old: The bhāṣya holds that speech has meaning in its sounds (varṇa);
fix.new: The bhāṣya holds that the organ of speech (vāc) functions only in producing the sounds (varṇa);

fix.value: So by saṃyama on their distinction the yogin gains knowledge of the cries of all beings (sarva-bhūta-ruta-jñāna).

evidence: (a) 'tatra vāg varṇeṣv evārthavatī / śrotraṃ ca dhvanipariṇāmamātraviṣayam': the point is that the speech organ operates only on the phonemes, as the ear only on sound-modifications, while the word is grasped by the intellect; 'speech has meaning in its sounds' reversed the argument, since the bhāṣya then says each sound alone is 'apadasvarūpa'. (b) The closing result 'evaṃ tatpravibhāgasaṃyamād yoginaḥ sarvabhūtarutajñānaṃ saṃpadyate' was omitted. Rest (pada as one buddhi-presentation, saṃketa as itaretarādhyāsa, 'ya eṣāṃ pravibhāgajñaḥ sa sarvavit', the śvetate/śvetaḥ examples) faithful.

fix.old: it adds that where the first fruit is set in the second's place by one whose attention is elsewhere, the distinction 'this is earlier, this later' is not possible without the discrimination-born knowledge.
fix.new: it adds that when, while the knower's attention is elsewhere (anya-vyagra), the first fruit is moved into the second's place, the place being the same, the distinction 'this is earlier, this later' cannot be made. How then? The place together with the moment of the earlier fruit differs from the place together with the moment of the later, and the two fruits differ by their experience of their own place-and-moment. By this example, when an atom alike in class, characteristic and place takes the place of an earlier atom, the masterful yogin (īśvara yogin), having directly perceived the earlier atom's place together with its moment, has the cognition of their otherness from the difference of the co-present moment.

evidence: Low-confidence entry checked line by line. (a) 'yadā tu pūrvam āmalakam anyavyagrasya jñātur uttaradeśa upāvartyate': the fruit is moved while the knower is distracted; the paraphrase made the distracted person the one who moves it. (b) The bhāṣya's own solution was omitted: 'pūrvāmalakasahakṣaṇo deśa uttarāmalakasahakṣaṇād deśād bhinnaḥ ... paramāṇos tulyajātilakṣaṇadeśasya ... sahakṣaṇabhedāt tayor īśvarasya yogino 'nyatvapratyayo bhavati'. The cow/mare, kālākṣī/svastimatī and myrobalan examples are faithful.

fix.old: Others explain that the ultimate particulars (antyā viśeṣāḥ) produce the notion of otherness, and there too difference of place and characteristic, and difference of body-form, obstruction and class, are the reason for otherness; difference of moment is accessible only to the yogin's intellect. Hence, the bhāṣya says, Vārṣagaṇya declared that where there is no difference of form, obstruction and class, there is no primary separateness (mūla-pṛthaktva).
fix.new: Others (apare) explain that it is the ultimate particulars (antyā viśeṣāḥ) that produce the notion of otherness. The bhāṣya answers: even there, difference of place and characteristic, and difference of form, interval (vyavadhi) and class, is the reason for otherness, while difference of moment is accessible only to the yogin's intellect; hence it has been said, 'where there is no difference of form, interval and class, there is no root-separateness (mūla-pṛthaktva)': so Vārṣagaṇya.
